headline: Court frames graft charges against Matiur, ex-NBR official linked to Tk 15 lakh goat
summary: Former NBR member Matiur Rahman faces trial for allegedly amassing illegal wealth of Tk 5.4 crore and concealing assets worth Tk 1.27 crore.
details: A Dhaka court has framed charges against former National Board of Revenue (NBR) member Matiur Rahman in a corruption case. He is accused of amassing illegal wealth of Tk 5.4 crore and concealing assets worth Tk 1.27 crore.
Matiur, who is currently in jail, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out by Judge BM Tarikul Kabir of the Divisional Special Judge's Court.
The court has scheduled September 14 for the recording of testimony from prosecution witnesses. Matiur was brought from prison to the court for the proceedings.
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) filed the case on December 15, 2024, and submitted the charge sheet on February 3 this year.
Matiur was arrested by the Detective Branch of Dhaka Metropolitan Police on January 15, 2025, while serving as president of the NBR's Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribunal.
He first gained public notoriety in June 2024 after a video of his son purchasing a goat for Tk 15 lakh ahead of Eid went viral, sparking scrutiny of the family's luxury assets.
According to ACC lawyers, two additional corruption cases involving Matiur are currently under investigation.
caption:
From a Tk 15 lakh goat to a Tk 5.4 crore corruption case. Former NBR official Matiur Rahman now faces trial.

A Dhaka court has framed charges against former National Board of Revenue (NBR) member Matiur Rahman in a corruption case. He is accused of amassing illegal wealth of Tk 5.4 crore and concealing assets worth Tk 1.27 crore.

Matiur, who is currently in jail, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out by Judge BM Tarikul Kabir of the Divisional Special Judge's Court.

The court has scheduled September 14 for the recording of testimony from prosecution witnesses. Matiur was brought from prison to the court for the proceedings.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) filed the case on December 15, 2024, and submitted the charge sheet on February 3 this year.

Matiur was arrested by the Detective Branch of Dhaka Metropolitan Police on January 15, 2025, while serving as president of the NBR's Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribunal.

He first gained public notoriety in June 2024 after a video of his son purchasing a goat for Tk 15 lakh ahead of Eid went viral, sparking scrutiny of the family's luxury assets.

According to ACC lawyers, two additional corruption cases involving Matiur are currently under investigation.
